Showcase extension: the Synth section (three layers A/B/C, each with its own effect chain) with the Analog waveform list, category-correct Osc Ctrl per waveform family, and the full filter/envelope graph feeding real oscillators; rendered tests prove waveform families are audibly distinct and Osc Ctrl measurably changes the spectrum. Manual-canonical additions: the Osc Pitch view (manual p. 28 Pitch and Fine Tune: PITCH/SMP latches the Synth OLED dials onto -24..+24 semitones + ±50 cents per layer, applied as a detune offset on every Analog source oscillator and through the Samples playbackRate pitch factor, live-retargeting sounding voices) and Sound Init as Shift + Waveform Select (manual p. 37 — the panel's ONE red-framed button; no separate control). Optional scope (spec.scope.optional): Sound Init's reset semantics (resets a layer's sound params, preserving enable/level/octave/zone); four new oscillator categories appended after FM-H — Sub Osc (real square sub-oscillator one octave down, Osc Ctrl = sub level), Shape (Shape Pulse: PeriodicWave duty follows Osc Ctrl, rebuilt on quantized steps like Sync) plus the separate ShapeSine category (Shape Sine: sine through a live-drive wavefolding waveshaper), Wave (Wave Organ/Wave Formant: two fixed digital PeriodicWaves, Osc Ctrl has no effect like Pure), and FM-I (FM 2-op B: identical 2-op FM to FM-H but a 1.414 inharmonic modulator ratio); and a per-layer Samples mode (Analog<->Samples cycle) that swaps the oscillator voice for AudioBufferSource playback from two bundled sample sets (src/audio/library.ts SYNTH_SAMPLE_SETS, provenance in library.test.ts), reusing the WAVE list/dial to pick the set with the filter/envelopes/unison/vibrato graph unchanged.

Showcase extension: the filter (type/freq/res/envelope amount) and all three envelopes (amp/filter/osc) drive real audible shaping — rendered tests show filter sweep brightness, envelope-driven amplitude contour, and osc-envelope pitch sweep. Optional scope (spec.scope.optional): two filter types appended to the same FILTER TYPE cycle — LP M (a declared ladder-style approximation: two cascaded lowpass stages with the second stage's resonance mapped 1.5x hotter, plus a fixed tanh k=1.5 pre-shaper always active for this type) and LP+HP (a lowpass at the cutoff in series with a highpass fixed 2 octaves below it, a wider/shallower emphasis than BP's single resonant stage) — both proven measurably distinct from LP24/BP at identical settings in rendered tests.

One AudioContext, per-layer voice buses, documented unit order asserted through real node connectivity, single master gain → limiter → one destination, ramped (click-free) automation, full dispose teardown.

Focus follows layer, panel A/B/Group cycling with LEDs, Group copy-on-entry, Shift+On Global for Delay/Comp/Reverb, on/bypass crossfades, dry/wet, All FX Off, delay feedback loop (repeats only) with selectable filter, To Rotary routing post-reverb into the single rotary instance, rotary speed/stop inertia, tap tempo.

The sealed Phase 1 surface (layout, control inventory, chassis geometry) still passes untouched by every later showcase extension.

Part 3 of the Synth engine, voice half (spec: nord-stage-4.synth.json voice): per-layer voice.mode (Poly/Mono/Legato), priority (Off/Low/High), glide (0..127, constant-rate portamento via setTargetAtTime), unison (Off/1/2/3, detuned duplicate oscillator pairs reusing the piano unison pattern), and vibrato (Off/On/Wheel, a per-layer pitch LFO whose depth is vibratoAmount-scaled or the live mod-wheel/pedal position scaled by vibratoAmount). Mono always retriggers the single sounding voice's envelope on a new note; Legato reuses the sounding voice and glides its oscillator frequencies in place (no envelope retrigger, no new nodes) when notes overlap; priority Low/High makes the lower/higher of two held notes win the sounding voice while the loser waits on a held-note stack, and releasing the winner returns to the next-priority held note. VOICE MODE (Shift = priority), GLIDE, SYNTH UNISON and VIBRATO MODE are now functional. Rendered tests prove a Legato glide slides pitch continuously (zero-crossing rate rises across the glide) rather than stepping. Optional scope (spec.scope.optional): the vibrato cycle now includes Delayed (per-voice depth ramps 0->full over ~700ms via a dedicated per-voice gain stage inserted between the shared per-layer depth gain and each sounding voice's targets, so new notes get their own onset time without disturbing already-sounding voices) and Pedal (depth follows state.morphValues.pedal live, exactly mirroring Wheel's mod-wheel following) — Aftertouch stays excluded (no browser aftertouch input). The VIBRATO MENU button (spec voice.vibrato.menu: Rate 2.0-8.0 Hz linear, Amount displayed 0-10) is now functional: it latches the Synth OLED dials 1/2 onto per-layer Rate/Amount editing (mutually exclusive with the AMP/FILTER/OSC envelope dial-repurposing), the vibrato LFO oscillator's frequency follows the mapped Rate directly, and depth scales with the mapped Amount across every mode including Wheel/Pedal/Delayed. A pre-existing snapshot missing voice.vibratoRate backfills to the prior fixed-rate default (~5.5 Hz) via the same normalizeSynthLayer path used for other post-hoc synth fields.

Part 3 of the Synth engine, arpeggiator half (spec: nord-stage-4.synth.json arpeggiatorGate): a section-level scheduler on the injected timer boundary (self-rescheduling setTimeout chain, cleared on ARP RUN off/dispose), rate 0..127 -> 30..300 quarter-note BPM or the master clock when synced (Shift + ARP RUN). Arp mode steps through the held-note set expanded over 1..4 octaves (RANGE) in Up/Down/Up-Down/Random order (Shift + ARP MODE), Random drawn from a deterministic xorshift RNG reseeded on every run-start; Poly mode retriggers every held note each step; Gate mode does not retrigger at all — it pulses the sounding voices' gain between full and a hardness floor (RANGE knob repurposed) with no new voices. KB HOLD keeps the held-note set (and the arp's cycle through it) alive after physical key-up; Panic and ARP RUN off clear it. Every step plays through the normal startSynthVoice path so zones and sustain stay consistent. ARP RUN, ARP MODE, ARP RATE, ARP RANGE and KB HOLD are now functional. Because the offline render harness's timer boundary is a no-op (voice-cleanup GC only), the rendered proof drives the exact onset sequence the scheduler produces through the same voice path at two different BPMs and shows a different onset count in the same window — the fake-level tests exercise the real scheduler class directly via injectable ManualTimers.

A program capturing every functional engine — Piano, Organ, all three Synth layers (each with its own independent effect chain now, spec: "their own effect chains"), splits, scenes, morphs, the arpeggiator/gate and KB Hold — round-trips completely through Store/reload, and the restored state drives a real note through the engine without falling back.
